summary: The fish half is covered cross-sectionally: ICES DATRAS serves open age–length records for plaice and haddock by survey, year and quarter (e.g., NS-IBTS 2022 Q3: 3,185 plaice and 5,633 haddock aged fish), which gives two seasonal points per year (Q1/Q3) but not the same individuals. The human half has only the Berkeley Growth Study (93 children, 31 ages 1–18) openly available, which lacks measurement dates and is annual after age 8. No open dataset gives the same individuals measured several times a year across adolescence with calendar dates.
next_step: Pre-register a DATRAS test on Q1-vs-Q3 length-at-age increments by cohort for plaice and haddock (needs the HH table for haul dates); for humans, locate a dated longitudinal series (e.g., school-measurement archives) or treat the human part as a gap.
obstacles_confirmed: Cross-sectional fish surveys do not track the same individuals.
Open human longitudinal records with fine seasonal resolution are limited.
Open human series rarely repeat the same individuals at half-year intervals across adolescence.
